notes.text: I — The Messiah. My messenger - John the Baptist. The Lord - The Messiah. Whom ye seek - Whom ye, who truly fear God, long and wait for. Suddenly come - After the coming of his fore- runner. To his temple - That which was the second temple at Jerusalem, lately built by Zerubbabel and Joshua. The messenger - The angel of the covenant, the Messiah, in whose blood the covenant between God and man was confirmed. Whom ye delight in - You Jews, among whom, few there are, who do not please themselves to think of his coming, tho' from various motives.

Abide — Who shall be able to stand under the weight of those crosses which in that day, will fall on all sorts of men? The day - This day was from his preaching, 'till the utter destruction of Jerusalem, about seventy years after the birth of Christ. A refiner's fire - Some are like metals, which nothing but a fierce fire can purge, such fire shall the troubles of these days be. Fuller's soap - As boiling waters, into which, spotted cloaths are thrown, and as the rubbing of them with soap; so that day will prove to all, a day of great trial, to purge and refine.

He shall fit — As resolved to attend his work and finish it. He shall purify - The effect of this fiery trial, shall be the thorough cleansing of the persons that are to pass through it. Sons of Levi - Either the Jewish Levites, or all Christians, who are made priests unto God. In righteousness - That they may offer themselves, their souls and bodies to God, in righteousness and true holiness.
The offerings — The services and duties of the whole Christian church. Pleasant - Well pleasing to him.

They-That constantly abide in thy house; the priests and Levites, or other devout Jews who were there perpetually, as Anna, Luke ii, 36-37. They will — They are continually employed in that blessed work.
Whose strength — Who trusteth in thee as his only strength. Thy ways - Blessed are they whose hearts are set upon Zion and their journey is thither.

Baca — A dry valley in the way to Jerusalem, here put for all places of like nature. Make a well - They dig divers little pits or wells in it for their relief. The rain - God recompenses their diligence with his blessing, sending rain wherewith they may be filled.
They go — They grow stronger and stronger. Appeareth - This is added as the blessed fruit of their long and tedious journey.
Look — Cast a favourable eye towards him. Anointed - Of me, who though a vile sinner, am thine anointed king.
Than dwell — In the greatest glory and plenty.

A sun — To enlighten and quicken, and direct and comfort his people. Shield - To save his people from all their enemies. Grace - His favour, which is better than life. Glory - The honour which comes from God here, and eternal glory. A recital of past, and prayer for present mercy, ver. 1-7. A prediction of a favourable answer, ver. 8-13. To the chief musician, A psalm for the sons of Korah.

glossa.text: *How lovely.* Behold how great the warfare. *For the sparrow,* how secure.

*For the sparrow,* etc. ((AUG.)) To two he renders two: *the heart* as *the sparrow; the flesh* as *the turtle,* to which he gives also *young ones:* with the heart we think upon God, as the sparrow flies to the house; with the flesh we do works. ((CASS.)) As the sparrow forsakes the woods, and rejoices when a house is found, where it fears no snares: so the soul rejoices, while it knows that a house is prepared for it in heaven. The spirit, which is as a sparrow flying on high, reaching towards God himself. *A nest, etc.* ((AUG.)) *A nest* for a time, *a house* true unto eternity. By the nest therefore he means faith, and the conformity of the sacraments of the Church, which nest the turtle seeks, that she may lay up her young. For she does not cast them anywhere, but in the nest of the Church she does good works wholesomely, for which she is saved: wherein she differs from others who do works, but not in the nest of faith. For the pagans also do works, they clothe the naked, etc., and heretics do many things: but not in the nest of the Church, and therefore they are trodden down, they are not preserved. This flesh is the woman, by whom the sparrow is seduced, but she shall be saved by the bearing of works, if in the nest, that is, if she shall have persevered in faith. But God supplies that whereof the nest may be made, for he clothed himself with the hay of the flesh that he might come to thee. *Thy altars, O Lord.* ((CASS.)) Where souls feast at the heavenly banquet, where the soul may rejoice as in a house. ((AUG.)) And the flesh lays up its works, whence: Blessed are they who, etc., where he shows to what beatitude the warfare leads.

*Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord; for ever and ever they shall praise thee.* ((AUG.)) This the good have already, namely, that they dwell in thy house. There follows: *For ever and ever they shall praise thee.* This is the whole business of the saints there: there is no necessity there, which is the mother of all human actions, for whom do they do anything there, where none are in need; they have therefore and they act, whence they are blessed. But every blessed one is called blessed by having or by acting.
*Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: he hath disposed ascensions in his heart.* ((CASS.)) By what help one may come to the house.

*In the vale of tears.* ((CASS.)) The vale of tears is the humility of one repenting. ((AUG.)) But whence the weeping: because he afflicted us with the law, through which we knew that sin fights against the spirit, and we groan, namely how we may come to the place which he has appointed, by his power and help assuredly. *In the place which he hath appointed. For he shall give a blessing.* Which cannot be set forth, which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, that is, the kingdom to come, which God has disposed and ordained, that it may be come to by degrees.
*O Lord God of hosts.* ((CASS.)) He prays and humbles himself for the obtaining of this help. *God of Jacob.* ((AUG.)) Whom thou madest Israel by appearing to him, so make me also Israel.

*Look upon the face,* etc. For he himself speaks in us, whence the Apostle: *Do you seek a proof of him that speaketh in me, Christ!* And he is received in us, as he says, *He that receiveth you, receiveth me. Look.* The Father always looks upon Christ. ((CASS.)) But make him to be looked upon by the nations *ventibus* through the presence of the incarnation: or, thus by the face we become known to others. ((AUG.)) *Look* therefore *upon the face,* that is, make Christ known to all, that we may be able to go from virtue to virtue

*One day.* Unchangeable, namely without rising and setting, to which yesterday does not yield, which tomorrow does not press upon. *Above thousands,* above the infinite present days, which have an end. For which cause *I have chosen,* though I might reign, *to be abject* in the opinion of men, *in the house,* in the Church, *Behold how sweet it is, to be pressed by the burden of the winepress.*

*Because mercy.* ((CASS.)) Therefore I had rather be in the house of God than elsewhere, because in it he gives mercy, by which he justifies, after the truth of the promised reward. But to whom? to those who walk in innocence.
*O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that hopeth,* etc. Thou who dost such great things, which cannot be told.

notes.text: Since then these children partake of flesh and blood — Of human nature with all its infirmities. He also in like manner took part of the same; that through his own death he might destroy the tyranny of him that had, by God's permission, the power of death with regard to the ungodly. Death is the devil's servant and serjeant, delivering to him those whom he seizes in sin. That is, the devil - The power was manifest to all; but who exerted it, they saw not.

And deliver them, as many as through fear of death were all their lifetime, till then, subject to bondage — Every man who fears death is subject to bondage; is in a slavish, uncomfortable state. And every man fears death, more or less, who knows not Christ: death is unwelcome to him, if he knows what death is. But he delivers all true believers from this bondage.

For verily he taketh not hold of angels — He does not take their nature upon him. But he taketh hold of the seed of Abraham - He takes human nature upon him. St. Paul says the seed of Abraham, rather than the seed of Adam, because to Abraham was the promise made.

Wherefore it behoved him — It was highly fit and proper, yea, necessary, in order to his design of redeeming them. To be made in all things - That essentially pertain to human nature, and in all sufferings and temptations. Like his brethren -- this is a recapitulation of all that goes before: the sum of all that follows is added immediately. That he might be a merciful and faithful High Priest-Merciful toward sinners; faithful toward God. A priest or high priest is one who has a right of approaching God, and of bringing others to him. Faithful is treated of, chap. iii, 2, &c., with its use; merciful, chap. iv, 14, &c., with the use also; High Priest, chap. v, 4, &c., chap. vii, 1, &c. The use is added from chap. x, 19. In things pertaining to God, to expiate the sins of the people - Offering up their sacrifices and prayers to God; deriving God's grace, peace, and blessings upon them.
For in that he hath suffered being tempted himself he is able to succor them that are tempted — That is, he has given a manifest, demonstrative proof that he is able so to do.

glossa.text: *Because therefore.* As if: Since all were of one, and because the children who were to be sanctified had communicated in flesh, that is, were men of soul and body, which is taken by the blood, corruptible; therefore *he also,* Christ. *He partook of the same,* namely the children, or *of the same,* that is, of flesh and blood, and this in like manner, that is, passible and mortal, that he might be able to die, and so destroy the devil, and through death make void the law, and by grace make free the Jews who through fear of punishments were slaves of the law. *Through death.* A marvel, what? Death was the arms whereby the devil conquered, and by it the devil was conquered by Christ.

*Nowhere.* He partook of the same that he might sanctify men. And rightly is this cause added, because if he were not to deliver them, he would not partake with them. Which appears in the angels, because nowhere, that is, in no scripture, is he read to have taken hold of angels. *He taketh hold.* The Apostle said: *he taketh hold,* and not *he took up,* as if: He overtook one fleeing far off. In which the dignity of human nature can be understood, and the mercy and grace wherewith he did this, and the care which he had for us. For human nature fleeing before him, and fleeing far off (for we were far off); pursuing he took hold of it, not to the angelic, but to human nature was this dignity given, that God should be joined to it in one person.
*In all things.* Because he was born, brought up, he grew; he suffered, he died. He who above was called the figure of the Father's substance.

*For in that.* That is, in the flesh which he took he suffered many cruel things. And he knows by experience what that tribulation of those who suffer is. *Who are tempted.* God tempts that he may prove, the devil that he may deceive, man that he may know what he knows not.

notes.text: The days — The forty days prescribed, Lev. xii, 2, 4.
Exod. xiii, 2.
A pair of turtle doves, or two young pigeons — This offering sufficed for the poor. Lev. xii, 8.
The consolation of Israel — A common phrase for the Messiah, who was to be the everlasting consolation of the Israel of God. The Holy Ghost was upon him - That is, he was a prophet.
By the Spirit — By a particular Revelation or impulse from him.
Thy salvation — Thy Christ, thy saviour.
And the glory of thy people Israel — For after the Gentiles are enlightened, all Israel shall be saved.
Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken — For they did not thoroughly understand them.

Simeon blessed them — Joseph and Mary. This child is set for the fall and rising again of many - That is, he will be a savour of death to some, to unbelievers: a savour of life to others, to believers: and for a sign which shall be spoken against - A sign from God, yet rejected of men: but the time for declaring this at large was not yet come: that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed - The event will be, that by means of that contradiction, the inmost thoughts of many, whether good or bad, will be made manifest.
A sword shall pierce through thy own soul — So it did, when he suffered: particularly at his crucifixion.

Fourscore and four years — These were the years of her life, not her widowhood only. Who departed not from the temple - Who attended there at all the stated hours of prayer. But served God with fastings and prayers - Even at that age. Night and day - That is, spending therein a considerable part of the night, as well as of the day.

To all that were waiting for redemption — The scepter now appeared to be departing from Judah, though it was not actually gone: Daniel's weeks were plainly near their period. And the revival of the spirit of prophecy, together with the memorable occurrences relating to the birth of John the Baptist, and of Jesus, could not but encourage and quicken the expectation of pious persons at this time. Let the example of these aged saints animate those, whose hoary heads, like theirs, are a crown of glory, being found in the way of righteousness. Let those venerable lips, so soon to be silent in the grave, be now employed in the praises of their Redeemer. Let them labour to leave those behind, to whom Christ will be as precious as he has been to them; and who will be waiting for God's salvation, when they are gone to enjoy it.

And the child grew — In bodily strength and stature; and waxed strong in spirit - The powers of his human mind daily improved; filled with wisdom - By the light of the indwelling Spirit, which gradually opened itself in his soul; and the grace of God was upon him - That is, the peculiar favour of God rested upon him, even as man.

glossa.text: *They carried him.* The little ones who from the whole kingdom of the Jews were carried to the temple, if they were of the tribe of Levi, were kept back perpetually for the ministry of the house. If of another tribe, the firstborn were redeemed by a price given by their parents, to be carried back to their own homes.
*As it is written. ((BEDA.))* It is written in the law: *A woman who, having received,* etc., *as far as* she enters upon the joys of heavenly blessedness with the fruits of good works.
*A pair of turtledoves. ((ID.))* This was the offering of the poor, who were not able to offer a lamb, so that in all things the humility of the Lord might be plain.

*And behold there was a man.* Not only the angels, but every age and sex render testimony to the child that is born. And as he was foretold by the faithful of all ages, so at his coming he is proclaimed with the praise of all the saints.

*The child.* Since boyhood begins after the seven years of infancy, Jesus is frequently called a child, not so much for his age as for his service; whence the Prophet: *Behold my child,* because *the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister ((Isa. XLII)).*

*Now thou dost dismiss thy servant. ((AMBR.))* He who wishes to be dismissed, let him come into Jerusalem, etc., *as far as* then he shall be dismissed so that he may not see death, because he had seen life.

*Behold this child is set.* For the ruin of those who had stood, and the resurrection of those who had fallen; or for the ruin of vices, and for the resurrection of virtues. Not in himself alone, but in his preachers also is he set for ruin and resurrection; whence the Apostle: *We are the good odour of Christ unto God, in them that are saved, and in them that perish.* For by the good odour some are saved, others perish ((II Cor. II)).

*A sword. ((BEDA.))* The sorrow of the Lord's passion, etc., *as far as* she beholds the cockle springing up.

*That may be revealed.* Before, it was uncertain which of the Jews would receive the grace of Christ, and which would spit upon it: but at the hearing of the nativity the thoughts are revealed, and Herod and others are troubled, while certain men come to the teaching of Christ.

*And there was Anna,* etc. Because through a man and a woman the life of the whole world was lost, in the testimony of life returning through Christ Anna is joined to Simeon. It agrees with the mysteries of the Church that Anna is interpreted grace, who is the daughter of Phanuel, who is called the face of God; whence above: *The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us ((Psal. IV))*. *Of the tribe of Aser.* That is, of the blessed, she is descended, from him who among the twelve patriarchs is eighth in the order of birth, on account of the mystery of the resurrection. There are five Annas. The first the mother of Samuel, the second the wife of Raguel, the third the mother of Tobias, the fourth the daughter of Phanuel, the fifth the mother of Mary.

*She had advanced in days. ((BEDA.))* According to the history, Anna, and of a devout manner of life, etc., *as far as* they are multiplied on account of the apostolic teaching.

*To all who,* etc. To all the faithful who, weighed down by the yoke of the foreigner Herod, were awaiting the deliverance of the city and of the people, she promised through the coming of Christ a redemption close at hand from the tyranny of the stranger.
*And the child. ((BEDA.))* In that he was a child, etc., *as far as* he had begun to be made man, he was perfect as God.

registers.label: Spare
lines: How lovely is your dwelling place, O Lord of hosts.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
A light for revelation, and glory for your people.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Two old people have waited their whole lives in the temple for one promise to come true.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
And here it is — carried in by a poor young couple — a forty-day-old child.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
Simeon takes him up and is ready, at last, to go in peace.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
A light to the nations and a glory to God's people, longed-for and finally here.
My eyes have seen your salvation; now let your servant go in peace!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Two elders wait a lifetime in the temple.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
A poor couple carries in the long-awaited child.
My eyes have seen your salvation.
A light to the nations; now we go in peace.
My eyes have seen your salvation. Amen.
